h02.answer_text: Coca‑Cola (ticker KO) grew revenue the fastest among the three companies, posting an 11 % year‑over‑year increase in fiscal 2022 (revenue growth rate ≈ 0.1125).  Its 2022 Form 10‑K explains that the revenue rise was driven by several factors: a 5 % increase in concentrate sales volume, favorable price, product and geographic mix that added about 11 % to revenue, modest contributions from acquisitions and divestitures, and a positive channel and package‑mix effect.  Pricing initiatives also supported growth, while foreign‑currency movements were a headwind.

citations.ref:
with rev as (
  select
    c.name as company_name,
    c.ticker as ticker,
    max(case when am.period_end_year = 2022 then am.value end) as rev_2022,
    max(case when am.period_end_year = 2021 then am.value end) as rev_2021
  from cn_4509b5c383744bb6.companies c
  join cn_4509b5c383744bb6.annual_metrics am
    on am.ticker = c.ticker
  where c.ticker in ('KO','PEP','GIS')
    and am.metric = 'revenue'
    and am.period_end_year in (2021, 2022)
    and am.unit = 'USD'
  group by c.name, c.ticker
)
select
  rev.company_name,
  rev.ticker,
  (rev.rev_2022 - rev.rev_2021) / nullif(rev.rev_2021, 0) as revenue_growth_rate
from rev
order by revenue_growth_rate desc
limit 1

h06.answer_text: CVS Health had the larger revenue in fiscal 2022, reporting $322.5 billion versus Johnson & Johnson’s $78.7 billion. CVS’s 2022 Form 10‑K describes its business as organized into three operating segments—Health Care Benefits, Pharmacy Services, and Retail/LTC—plus a Corporate/Other segment. The Health Care Benefits segment provides pharmacy‑benefit management and related services; Pharmacy Services offers pharmacy‑benefit management, mail‑order and specialty pharmacy services; Retail/LTC includes its more than 9,000 retail locations, MinuteClinic sites and long‑term‑care pharmacies. The Corporate/Other segment consists of corporate‑level functions and legacy products. The company’s chief operating decision maker evaluates segment performance primarily using adjusted operating income.

Netflix’s consolidated revenue grew steadily from $6.78 billion in fiscal 2015 to $31.62 billion in fiscal 2022. The 2017 Form 10‑K outlines Netflix’s streaming strategy as a focus on globally expanding its streaming membership business while maintaining profit‑margin targets. The company emphasizes continuously improving the member experience by expanding streaming content—especially original programming—enhancing the user interface, and extending the service to more internet‑connected screens. It also highlights the importance of building consumer awareness of streaming offerings, growing international memberships (which accounted for 44% of revenue in 2017), and strengthening relationships with partners to broaden distribution across devices.

h23.answer_text:
Ulta Beauty’s net income rose from $658.6 million in fiscal 2019 to $1.242 billion in fiscal 2023, an increase of roughly $584 million (about 89%). After a dip to $175.8 million in 2021, net income rebounded to $985.8 million in 2022 and continued to grow in 2023.

The 2023 Form 10‑K describes the Ultamate Rewards loyalty program as a best‑in‑class system that lets members earn points for every dollar spent in Ulta stores, on Ulta.com, at Ulta Beauty at Target, and through co‑branded or private‑label credit cards. Points are valid for at least one year and can be redeemed for discounts on any product or service. Revenue from earned points is deferred and recognized only when points are redeemed or expire. The company notes that more than 95% of total sales are generated by its 40.2 million active members, providing deep customer insights and higher spend per visit.
